signs.text: Prince Edward Battery|Built 1805 to defend the harbour|Now fires mostly for royal birthdays
signs.why: Low interpretive sign by the roadway at the battery (sign itself not seen). The battery dates from 1805; today the PEI Regiment fires royal salutes there (21 guns for the King, Sept 2022). Check the "only ever salutes" implication before using.

signs.text: MULTI-USE PATH|Walk, run, cycle, skate, scoot|Cyclists: ring before passing|Walkers: the boardwalk is right there
signs.why: The real sign is a row of green-ringed pictograms (skater, skateboard, bike, scooter, stroller, dog, walker, runner) on a white panel fixed to the planter; the city has asked walkers for years to use the boardwalk instead

signs.text: Victoria Park|Forty hectares of park|One small parking lot
signs.why: Park entrance at Kent and West streets by Beaconsfield; council has heard for years that the pool, playground and ball fields leave no parking in the evenings

signs.text: Confederation Landing|The delegates came ashore here in 1864|The Island joined in 1873
signs.why: Park sign at the Great George/Water Street side: PEI hosted the 1864 conference and then stayed out for nine years

landmark_fixes.name: Battery lookout building, Victoria Park
landmark_fixes.change: Not a closed shed: an open timber viewing deck (weathered grey-brown, plank railing, straight stair down the back) about 2.5 m up on the battery's grassy earthwork. No walls, no roof. Also: the battery is five wheeled guns plus three 32-pounders on wooden slide carriages, and a stone magazine (heritage register).

landmark_fixes.name: Confederation Landing Park bandstand
landmark_fixes.change: Confirmed by photo: octagonal, grey shingled roof with an open lantern cupola, white posts; curved stone/concrete steps in front on red brick paving; a tall white flagpole with the Canada flag beside it and white swan-neck globe lamps round it (not black lanterns).

landmark_fixes.name: Port Charlottetown cruise terminal
landmark_fixes.change: Add: the big red maple-leaf photo sign outside on red brick pavers with sandstone blocks (new_models_needed); the hall inside has exposed timber trusses and hosted a 10-ft red-sand sculpture (2023). The apron where ships tie up has red sandstone riprap at the shore ends.

landmark_fixes.name: Kiwanis Dairy Bar
landmark_fixes.change: No change to the building; its picnic tables are given positions here (props).

landmark_fixes.name: Government House (Fanningbank)
landmark_fixes.change: Grounds have no perimeter fence in the aerial photos: open lawn to Terry Fox Drive and the harbour, a belt of big trees round it, a looped gravel drive, flagpole on the south lawn, and the formal garden of low box hedges east of the house (hedge lines given here). Portico photo shows dark shutters and a grey-white wooden front step.

landmark_fixes.name: Beaconsfield Historic House
landmark_fixes.change: Confirmed: golden yellow, grey patterned mansard, belvedere with cresting, wraparound veranda with fretwork, deep flower borders (irises, poppies, spiraea) on the lawn in front. A red-brick building shows close behind it. Five antique lamp posts on the grounds (props here).

name_checks.name: HEIFERS (first-pass sign for the COWS shop, landmark 251166162)
name_checks.evidence: "Happy Heifers Cafe & Ice Creamery" in Mill Spring, North Carolina (and "Heifer and the Hen" in Boulder). Not exact, but close: consider another name.

name_checks.name: Port Charlottetown (the maple-leaf sign and terminal)
name_checks.evidence: The real harbour authority. The new sign model uses the place name CHARLOTTETOWN only.

name_checks.name: Joseph A. Ghiz Memorial Park
name_checks.evidence: Named for a real premier: no sign with his name (the park's interpretive panel carries his portrait). Call it "the memorial park" if a sign is wanted.

new_models_needed.what: Splash pad: round concrete pad (about 12 m across) painted pale blue and yellow, with a few bright spray posts and arches (yellow, blue, green, 1.5-2.5 m) and flush ground jets; wet sheen in summer, dry and empty Sept-June

new_models_needed.why: Victoria Park splash pad beside the pool and playgrounds (open late June to September). Which OSM circle it is is a guess: the 13 m round "playground" 256072000; the 10 m blob 256072007 is the other candidate

new_models_needed.what: Battery earthwork and lookout: a grassy rampart mound about 2-3 m high, and on it an open timber viewing deck (about 4 x 4 m, 2.5 m up) with a plank railing and a straight timber stair down the back; this is what OSM 655355138 "Battery Lookout Building" is, not a closed shed
new_models_needed.size_m: mound 40 x 12 m, 2.5 m high; deck 4 x 4 m
new_models_needed.shape: raised earth bank with sloped sides; open deck on posts with rail and stair
new_models_needed.why: The battery reads as a low fort bank with the guns behind it; the deck is where people stand to watch the harbour

new_models_needed.what: 32-pounder on a wooden traversing carriage: black iron barrel 3 m long on a low timber slide carriage that runs on a curved iron rail (racer) set in the ground
new_models_needed.colours: black barrel #1b1b1b, red-brown or grey timber #6b4a35
new_models_needed.shape: long low slide with a barrel on top, pivot at the front
new_models_needed.why: Three of these stand at the battery beside the wheeled field guns; cannon props stand in for now

new_models_needed.what: Floating dock: cream/off-white moulded plastic dock sections (EZ Dock type) with black connector pins in a grid, sitting 0.3 m above the water, joined to the wharf by an aluminium gangway ramp with white rails
new_models_needed.shape: flat platform on the water; ramp 1 m wide with rails
new_models_needed.why: The floating food court and the marina fingers at Peake's Quay; same kind at the Victoria Park paddle dock

street_feel: Two lamp styles on the waterfront: Confederation Landing and the marina promenade by Peake's Quay have WHITE swan-neck posts with white globes; the west boardwalk (culinary institute), Victoria Park, the multi-use path and the battery have the BLACK single-lantern heritage lamp. The many heritage_lamps placed round Confederation Landing should be the white style.

Benches everywhere on the waterfront are the same: black cast-iron scroll ends with pale/natural wood slats, many with a small memorial plaque on the back rail. They sit on the grass beside the boardwalk facing the water.
Bins: dark green plastic barrel bins with a domed lid in Victoria Park; brown slatted-wood bins at the memorial park.

Victoria Park boardwalk: about 3 m (10 ft) wide grey timber deck, rebuilt 2015-19, with a raised timber edge and NO railing; on the harbour side red sandstone riprap straight down to the water; on the land side it runs right beside the roadway with parked cars. Joggers, dogs, strollers; the floating paddle dock (cream plastic, white aluminium gangway rails) sticks out from it in summer.

Victoria Park inside: big old trees, dirt trails, a grassy pond (Dead Man's Pond), three ball diamonds with red-clay infields (Memorial Field lit, with a new home-run fence), the blue tennis courts behind tall chain-link (closed for repairs, 2025-26), the pool and bathhouse, the red-rubber accessible playground and an older blue-and-green one on gravel, a skate park, the yellow Kiwanis Dairy Bar by the water.

Prince Edward Battery: a grassy earth bank by the roadway, a white three-rail fence on top, a timber lookout deck, the old black guns pointing out to the harbour mouth; the PEI Regiment wheels in a modern howitzer for royal salutes.

Fanningbank: no fence, no gate guard; open lawns and a tree belt, a blue 'Private Residence' sign on a post, a box-hedge parterre with peonies, irises and day-lilies. Commissionaires from the government buildings patrol.

Confederation Landing: red brick paths and an oval, a lawn ringed with young maples, curved stone steps facing the bandstand, sandstone riprap at the marina edge, a timber boardwalk strip along the brick promenade with low hedges. Sunday market tents (orange, white, navy) round the oval in summer.

Peake's Wharf: the floating food court is a cream plastic dock with grey picnic tables and one red one, the red Chip Shack with its striped awning, a pale blue cabin, Nimrods' green hedge wall; aluminium ramps with white rails down to the floats. Unistone paving replaced the grass in 2021 and the boardwalks were all redone.

Port: wide concrete apron, red maple-leaf photo sign, the green steel gangway tower, yellow bollards, orange cruise lifeboats looming over the terminal on ship days (up to four ships; two anchor out and tender in).

Hillsborough Bridge path: on the south (harbour) side, two-way, asphalt, separated from four lanes of traffic by a steel guardrail on the causeways and a concrete barrier on the bridge deck, with a timber fence (vertical heavy boards/posts) on the water side of the causeways and a dark steel picket railing on the deck. Tall cobra-head street lights on the traffic side. Opened June 2021 ($4M). No suicide-prevention barrier was added. Cameras watch the bridge.
The Banks construction (15 Haviland, 2026-28): chain-link panels round a red-dirt lot by the west boardwalk, an excavator, the boardwalk detoured round it.

Memorial park (Joe Ghiz): flat lawn on the old rail yard, the Confederation Trail in red clay through it, red brick paths, petunia baskets on black poles, the red bike fix-it stand, a navy interpretive panel, a playground and a small basketball court, the IODE memorial fountain.
